entries.title: Time duration
entries.purpose: Time represents an elapsed simulation duration, stored as signed integer microseconds.
entries.example:
begin model.init event
    set pickupTime = 10 sec
    set cycleTime = 2 hour + 30 min
    set halfTime = cycleTime / 2
    print cycleTime to log
end
entries.notes: Time is different from Integer/Real. Time + Time and Time - Time yield Time; Time multiplied or divided by a number yields Time; Time / Time yields a ratio. Comparisons require two Time values. Logs render durations in seconds. Unit aliases sec/secs/second(s), min/mins/minute(s), hr/hrs/hour(s), day(s) are accepted. Plain numbers remain Integer/Real. Ordinary user-authored wait statements remain restricted by the current GRS syntax policy.

entries.title: GRS file
entries.purpose: Simulation Studio Model Logic source file.
entries.example:
begin model.init event
    print "ready" to log
end
entries.notes: GRS uses UTF-8 text. 2026-10-20: GRS was reduced to a minimal surface ahead of a full redesign. Supported: init events, model.snap, the 12 Vehicle events, if / else, while / for each, set / inc / dec, attributes, + - * / %, print ... to log, and all Humanoid events/functions. Anything else is rejected at Compile with GRS_REMOVED_SYNTAX.
entries.related: Init events, Vehicle event syntax, if / else, while, print to log

entries.title: Model snap
entries.purpose: Runs after a completed Model session snapshot boundary. The event observes the model at the exact committed simulation time, without creating a UI render timer.
entries.example:
begin model.init event
    set snapCount = 0
end
begin model.snap event
    inc snapCount by 1
    print "model snap", snapCount to log
end
entries.notes: The first event runs at simulation time 0 after Init. Thereafter one event runs for each successful forward ModelExecutionSession.advanceTo() call, after all physics modules finish. Re-reading the immutable snapshot, pausing, or advancing to the same time does not fire it again. Each module executes its own defined model.snap handler, if present. This is not triggered by Qt paint/repaint and it is not a request to save the project file. 'begin model snap event' is accepted as an alias. Normal GRS restrictions on wait and functions still apply.
entries.related: model.init, Time duration, print to log

entries.title: Init events
entries.purpose: Runs once at simulation time zero to initialize model values.
entries.syntax:
begin model.init event
    ...
end
begin OHT.init event
    ...
end
begin AMR.init event
    ...
end
begin Humanoid.init event
    ...
end
entries.example:
begin model.init event
    set count = 0
    print "model ready" to log
end
entries.notes: model.init runs once per model. OHT.init / AMR.init / Humanoid.init are the typed initializers used by Global Init.
entries.related: Global Init, set, print to log

entries.title: Global Init / default OHT AMR Humanoid
entries.purpose: Create the default OHT, AMR and Humanoid counts directly from one global initialization event.
entries.syntax:
begin model.init event
    vi_OHT = 10
    vi_Humanoid = 3
    vi_AMR = 3
end
entries.example:
begin model.init event
    vi_OHT = 10
    vi_Humanoid = 3
    vi_AMR = 3
end
begin OHT.init event
    set i = 0
    while i < vi_OHT
    begin
        inc i by 1
        print "OHT", i, " is initialized" to log
    end
end
begin Humanoid.init event
    set i = 0
    while i < vi_Humanoid
    begin
        inc i by 1
        print "Humanoid", i, " is initialized" to log
    end
end
begin AMR.init event
    set i = 0
    while i < vi_AMR
    begin
        inc i by 1
        print "AMR", i, " is initialized" to log
    end
end
entries.notes: New global-init script has exactly one model.init with three positive integer vi_* values and these three typed events. At Compile the already-placed drawing supplies one OHT rail Level and one AMR floor Level (each with two distinct Stations); scripted Job Source is used with no synthetic traffic. Existing C++ Core creates vi_OHT/vi_AMR vehicles. Three-dimensional default humanoids are created at a floor Station. The typed init events run once at simulation time zero and print to the Studio message log. Other legacy and previously declared auto-bound scripts retain their existing behavior. All five previous helper initializers are NOT required for this opt-in.
entries.related: model.init, OHT.init, AMR.init, Humanoid.init, print to log

entries.title: Vehicle event syntax
entries.purpose: Public Vehicle event syntax shared by OHT, AGV and AMR: vehicle. followed by the event name with underscores (pickup, setdown, speed_change, resume_to_drive, start_to_move, arrived_at_station, job_finished, job_selection, job_assigned, decelerate_to_destination, passing_station, destination_change). The old space form (begin Vehicle pickup event) was removed.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.job_assigned event
    print "job assigned" to log
end
entries.notes: The GRS compiler lowers these event declarations to the engine's existing internal callbacks. Existing project event keys still load for compatibility. The event actor Vehicle is available as this Vehicle. The same header works in OHT, AGV and AMR modules; steer change and for each ... in Vehicle are OHT only.
entries.related: Vehicle, Vehicle, OHT, AGV, AMR, GRS Events

entries.title: Vehicle pickup
entries.purpose: Arrives at the physical pickup boundary.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.pickup event
    print "Vehicle pickup" to log
end
entries.notes: The Load is loaded at the existing physical pickup boundary. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle setdown
entries.purpose: Arrives at the physical setdown boundary.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.setdown event
    print "Vehicle setdown" to log
end
entries.notes: The unloading completion occurs after the configured setdown dwell. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle speed change
entries.purpose: Physical Vehicle speed changes.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.speed_change event
    print "Vehicle speed change" to log
end
entries.notes: Uses existing engine speed transitions, not polling. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle resume to drive
entries.purpose: A stopped Vehicle starts driving again.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.resume_to_drive event
    print "Vehicle resume to drive" to log
end
entries.notes: Uses a real resume transition. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle start to move
entries.purpose: The Vehicle starts actual travel.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.start_to_move event
    print "Vehicle start to move" to log
end
entries.notes: Ignores the internal near-zero wake probe. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle job finished
entries.purpose: A physical ScheduleJob reaches its completed handoff.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.job_finished event
    print "Vehicle job finished" to log
end
entries.notes: Fires after setdown dwell. OHT: actor is the completed ScheduleJob (this Vehicle is its Vehicle). AMR / AGV: actor is the carrying Vehicle. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle job selection
entries.purpose: A live ScheduleJob becomes selected.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.job_selection event
    print "Vehicle job selection" to log
end
entries.notes: OHT: actor is the selected ScheduleJob; unchanged selection does not re-fire. AMR / AGV: actor is the Vehicle the Job was assigned to. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle decelerate to destination
entries.purpose: The Vehicle reaches the final prepared travel span.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.decelerate_to_destination event
    print "Vehicle decelerate to destination" to log
end
entries.notes: Fires on actual movement in the final span. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle arrived at station
entries.purpose: The Vehicle reaches its pickup or setdown Station.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.arrived_at_station event
    print "Vehicle arrived at station" to log
end
entries.notes: Fires once at the arrival boundary before the pickup/setdown event. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle job assigned
entries.purpose: An idle OHT begins its next Job or explicit travel.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.job_assigned event
    print "Vehicle job assigned" to log
end
entries.notes: 2026-10-17: fires on Idle-to-travel/Pickup transition; actor is the assigned Vehicle. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle passing station
entries.purpose: The OHT passes a Station on its route.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.passing_station event
    print "Vehicle passing station" to log
end
entries.notes: 2026-10-17: fires for each physically crossed Station, excluding departure; no fleet-wide polling. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT.

entries.title: Vehicle destination change
entries.purpose: The OHT starts a new travel leg toward its destination.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.destination_change event
    print "Vehicle destination change" to log
end
entries.notes: 2026-10-17: fires at travel-leg start (initial travel or post-pickup delivery), up to twice per Job. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.title: Vehicle OHT / AGV / AMR differences
entries.purpose: The vehicle.<event_name> header is the only spelling: there are no separate Def_OHT / Def_AGV / Def_AMR headers. It works in OHT, AGV (AMR Core Fixed Path) and AMR modules with the same 12 event names.
entries.example:
begin vehicle.passing_station event
    print "passing ", vehicle.passing_station_name to log
end
entries.notes: Observation is enabled only for events you implement and never changes physics. This Vehicle is the actor Vehicle. passing station radius for AMR / AGV is max(250 mm, body radius); vehicle.passing_station_name reads the station just passed. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT. for each ... in Vehicle is OHT only: an AMR / AGV module that uses it is rejected before the run.
entries.related: Vehicle, AMR, AGV, OHT, GRS Events

entries.title: Humanoid event syntax
entries.purpose: Humanoid uses the same 12 event names (begin humanoid.pickup event, ...). Job means humanoid_transfer; pickup/setdown fire when humanoid_pick/humanoid_place start.
entries.example:
begin humanoid.job_finished event
    print "done ", this Humanoid to log
end
entries.notes: this Humanoid is humanoid_self(); humanoid_event_place() reads the place just passed (within 400 mm) inside passing station. resume to drive occurs only in live walking. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT.

entries.title: Humanoid walk events (two-file global init)
entries.purpose: Run starts OHT 10, AMR 3 and Humanoid 3 and drives Humanoid 1 and 2 back and forth through physical floor Stations.
entries.example:
begin Humanoid walk resume event
    wait for 0.5 sec
end
begin Humanoid walk start event
    print this humanoid, " walk start now" to log
end
begin Humanoid arrived at station event
    if (current station = humanoid_1)
        dispatch this humanoid to humanoid_2
    else if (current station = humanoid_2)
        dispatch this humanoid to humanoid_1
end
entries.notes: Opt-in requires two GRS files: model_init.grs with vi_OHT, vi_AMR, vi_Humanoid and OHT.init, AMR.init, Humanoid.init; and humanoid_logic.grs with walk resume/start/arrived at station events. All three Init callbacks must complete across all modules before any regular t=0 event or initial humanoid walk begins. A waiting/failed Init rejects Run before simulation time advances. In model_init.grs the authored spwan Humanoid(1 or 2) to humanoid_1 or humanoid_2 is accepted as compatibility syntax. These compile to native humanoid_create, humanoid_walk_to, humanoid.arrived and a suspended 0.5-second wait. Each physical arrival triggers the next leg, without every-event polling. Humanoid 3 remains idle until explicitly dispatched; Job flows removed from this project are not auto restored. Existing auto-bound and explicitly declared module behavior is unchanged.
entries.related: Humanoid.init, humanoid.arrived, humanoid_create, humanoid_walk_to, print to log

entries.title: if / else if / else
entries.purpose: Executes conditional branches.
entries.syntax:
if <condition> then begin
    ...
end
else begin
    ...
end
entries.example:
if vehicle.id = 1 then begin
    print "first vehicle" to log
end
else begin
    print "other vehicle" to log
end
entries.notes: The AutoMod-style two-line form is also accepted: write if (condition) or else if (condition) and put begin on the next line. In conditions = is comparison.

entries.title: while
entries.purpose: Repeats a block while its condition is true.
entries.example:
set i = 0
while i < 5
begin
    inc i by 1
    print "i = ", i to log
end
entries.notes: The two-line form (while condition, then begin on the next line) is accepted.

entries.title: for each
entries.purpose: Iterates a list snapshot.
entries.syntax:
for each <item> in <list> do begin
    ...
end
entries.example:
for each v in Vehicle
begin
    print v to log
end
entries.notes: for each v in Vehicle iterates all OHT vehicles (OHT only). The list is evaluated once when the loop begins.

entries.title: break
entries.purpose: Leaves the innermost while / for each loop.
entries.example:
while i < 10
begin
    inc i by 1
    if i = 5 then begin
        break
    end
end
entries.notes: Only valid inside a loop.

entries.title: continue
entries.purpose: Skips to the next iteration of the innermost loop.
entries.example:
while i < 10
begin
    inc i by 1
    if i % 2 = 0 then begin
        continue
    end
    print i to log
end
entries.notes: Only valid inside a loop.

entries.title: print to log
entries.purpose: Writes text to the Studio message log.
entries.notes: Arguments are rendered in order. print ... to message was removed; use to log.

entries.title: set
entries.purpose: Assigns a variable or a writable attribute.
entries.notes: Custom attributes on Vehicle are script-side values and never overwrite physical Vehicle state.

entries.title: inc
entries.purpose: Increments a numeric variable or attribute.
entries.notes: Unwritten numeric values begin at 0.

entries.title: dec
entries.purpose: Decrements a numeric variable or attribute.
entries.notes: Unwritten numeric values begin at 0.

entries.title: vehicle.id
entries.purpose: Dense Vehicle identifier for the current Vehicle actor.
entries.notes: Read-only physical identity.

entries.title: vehicle.station / from / destination
entries.purpose: Reads the current Station, job source and job destination from the SimulationEngine snapshot.
entries.notes: Returns null when the corresponding Station is invalid/unset.

entries.title: vehicle.phase / status
entries.purpose: Returns the current physical phase as a string: idle, retrieving, pickup, moving or setdown.
entries.example:
if vehicle.phase = "idle" then begin
    print "idle vehicle ", vehicle.id to log
end
entries.notes: SimulationEngine remains the physical truth owner.

entries.title: operators
entries.purpose: Arithmetic, remainder, comparison and boolean operators.
entries.example:
set r = 7 % 3
if r = 1 and vehicle.id > 0 then begin
    print "remainder ", r to log
end
entries.notes: % is the remainder (modulo). Division or remainder by zero stops the current event with an error. In conditions = is comparison.

entries.title: vehicle / self
entries.purpose: Provides the current Vehicle actor surface and current actor custom-attribute surface.
entries.notes: Custom modeling state is script-side and does not overwrite physical Vehicle state.

entries.title: humanoid.color_fixed()
entries.purpose: Turns off the pose color change so every Humanoid keeps its original model color.
entries.notes: Call from model.init. Only the display color changes; motion, timing and results are unchanged. Implementation spelling: humanoid.color_fixed().

entries.title: Humanoid_Create(name, place | name, x_m, y_m)
entries.purpose: Creates a Humanoid at a Station/defined place or x/y (m).
entries.syntax: call Humanoid_Create(name, place | name, x_m, y_m)
entries.example: call Humanoid_Create(name, place | name, x_m, y_m)
entries.notes: Battery starts full. Spec: gigaroute/humanoid/humanoid_spec.hpp (175 cm adult male). Implementation spelling: humanoid_create().

entries.title: Humanoid_Define_Place(name, work_height_mm | name, x_m, y_m [, work_height_mm])
entries.purpose: Defines a named work place for humanoid_walk_to/pick/place. Station form (name, work_height_mm) takes position/level from the Station of that name, so no coordinates are written in GRS.
entries.syntax: call Humanoid_Define_Place(name, work_height_mm | name, x_m, y_m [, work_height_mm])
entries.example: call Humanoid_Define_Place(name, work_height_mm | name, x_m, y_m [, work_height_mm])
entries.notes: Defined places win over Station names. Default work height is 900 mm. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_place().

entries.title: Humanoid_Define_Obstacle(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, level_id [, z_min_m [, z_max_m]]])
entries.purpose: Defines a rectangular obstacle Humanoids walk around (optionally limited to a height range).
entries.syntax: call Humanoid_Define_Obstacle(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, level_id [, z_min_m [, z_max_m]]])
entries.example: call Humanoid_Define_Obstacle(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, level_id [, z_min_m [, z_max_m]]])
entries.notes: On a level with at least one obstacle, humanoid_walk_to/walk/transfer plan a detour (AMR grid A*, body half-width + 50 mm clearance) and use its length x route_factor. Levels without obstacles keep straight-line x route_factor. A walk with no route is rejected. Already planned walks are not re-planned. Height range (default floor to ceiling): an obstacle blocks a Humanoid only if z_max > 0.1 m and z_min < its height, so a low curb is stepped over and an overhead beam is walked under. AMR positions at request time are treated as temporary obstacles on the walk. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_obstacle().

entries.title: Humanoid_Remove_Obstacle(name)
entries.purpose: Removes an obstacle (true if it existed).
entries.notes: Affects walks requested afterwards. Implementation spelling: humanoid_remove_obstacle().

entries.title: Humanoid_Define_Zone(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, capacity [, level_id]])
entries.purpose: Defines a corridor/area that at most `capacity` (default 1) Humanoids may be walking through at once.
entries.syntax: call Humanoid_Define_Zone(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, capacity [, level_id]])
entries.example: call Humanoid_Define_Zone(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, capacity [, level_id]])
entries.notes: A Humanoid entering from outside waits at the entrance until the zone has room (first-requested first-served). Only walking time inside the zone is counted; standing Humanoids and other vehicle types do not occupy it. Zones on one level must not overlap. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_zone().

entries.title: Humanoid_Route_Distance(robot, place)
entries.purpose: Planned walking distance in m (obstacle detour x route_factor) without moving; -1 if unknown or unroutable.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_route_distance().

entries.title: Humanoid_Zone_Wait(robot)
entries.purpose: Total seconds the Humanoid has waited at zone entrances.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_zone_wait().

entries.title: Humanoid_Set(robot, parameter, value)
entries.purpose: Overrides one spec value for one Humanoid.
entries.notes: walk_speed/carry_speed/cart_speed/accel/decel are m/s(^2); turn_speed deg/s; payload_one_arm/payload_two_arm/item_mass kg; *_seconds, robot_time_factor, route_factor, battery_capacity_wh, battery_percent, *_power_w, low_battery_percent, mass_kg. Implementation spelling: humanoid_set().

entries.title: Humanoid_Spec([robot,] parameter)
entries.purpose: Returns a spec/body value (height_mm, shoulder_height_mm, max_reach_height_mm, forward_reach_mm, walk_speed, ...).
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_spec().

entries.title: Humanoid_Walk_To(robot, place)
entries.purpose: Turns and walks to a Station/defined place. Returns seconds.
entries.notes: Straight-line distance x route_factor with trapezoidal speed; carry/cart speeds apply automatically. Fires humanoid.arrived. Implementation spelling: humanoid_walk_to().

entries.title: Humanoid_Walk(robot, meters)
entries.purpose: Walks straight ahead. Returns seconds.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_walk().

entries.title: Humanoid_Dispatch_Async(robot, place)
entries.purpose: Starts a walk to a Station/defined place without suspending the caller. Returns seconds.
entries.notes: Same physical walk as humanoid_walk_to, but the calling GRS process continues; the next leg is driven by humanoid.arrived. Implementation spelling: humanoid_dispatch_async().

entries.title: Humanoid_Queue_Initial_Dispatch(robot, place)
entries.purpose: Registers an initial walk during Humanoid.init. Returns true.
entries.notes: Started at t=0 only after every OHT.init, AMR.init and Humanoid.init has completed (global Init barrier). Implementation spelling: humanoid_queue_initial_dispatch().

entries.title: Humanoid_Turn(robot, degrees)

entries.title: Humanoid_Pose(robot, pose)

entries.title: Humanoid_Pick(robot, item [, height_mm [, mass_kg]])

entries.purpose: Returns z (m) at the Humanoid position.

entries.title: Humanoid_Free_Hands(robot)

entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_free_hands().

entries.title: Humanoid_Battery(robot)

entries.notes: Fires humanoid.battery_low when crossing low_battery_percent. Implementation spelling: humanoid_battery().

entries.title: Humanoid_Busy(robot)
entries.purpose: Returns true until the current action ends.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_busy().

entries.title: Humanoid_State(robot)
entries.purpose: Returns the current action name or idle.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_state().

entries.title: Humanoid_Posture(robot)
entries.purpose: Returns the current posture name.
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_posture().

entries.title: Humanoid_Distance(robot)
entries.purpose: Returns walked distance (m).
entries.notes: Implemented runtime callable. Implementation spelling: humanoid_distance().

entries.title: Humanoid_Utilization(robot)

entries.title: Humanoid_Actions(robot)

entries.purpose: Returns the committed target angle of one Humanoid joint.

entries.title: vehicle.id [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the dense runtime Vehicle/Robot ID.
entries.notes: Type: Number. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Physical runtime identity; not a user-defined attribute.

entries.title: vehicle.station [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the current/last Station index.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Alias vehicle.location resolves to the same value.

entries.title: vehicle.from [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the current Job source Station index.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.destination [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the current destination Station index.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.phase [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the authoritative runtime phase/status text.
entries.notes: Type: String. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Alias vehicle.status resolves to the same value.

entries.title: vehicle.current_speed [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns authoritative current linear speed.
entries.notes: Type: Number (mm/s). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. OHT reads the Rail Vehicle motion speed; AMR reads the robot linear speed.

entries.title: vehicle.remaining_distance [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns remaining distance on the current route.
entries.notes: Type: Number (mm). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Zero is valid at a destination or when no route is active.

entries.title: vehicle.x [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current world X position.
entries.notes: Type: Number (mm). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.y [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current world Y position.
entries.notes: Type: Number (mm). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.heading [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current heading in radians.
entries.notes: Type: Number (rad) or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. OHT can return null only when a legacy snapshot has no authoritative heading.

entries.title: vehicle.rotating_in_place [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns true while the runtime is rotating in place.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.current_path [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the directed Rail Path ID currently occupied by the OHT.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. AMR free-floor motion has no equivalent Rail Path ID.

entries.title: vehicle.has_assigned_job [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns whether the physical OHT owns a real transport Job.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. This is physical Job ownership, not merely a script custom attribute.

entries.title: vehicle.service_remaining_seconds [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns remaining Pickup/Setdown service time.
entries.notes: Type: Number (s). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. Returns zero outside Pickup/Setdown.

entries.title: vehicle.service_duration_seconds [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns configured duration of the active Pickup/Setdown service phase.
entries.notes: Type: Number (s). Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. Returns zero outside Pickup/Setdown.

entries.title: vehicle.angular_speed [AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current AMR angular speed.
entries.notes: Type: Number (rad/s). Access: read-only. Modules: AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.z [AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current AMR 2.5D elevation.
entries.notes: Type: Number (mm). Access: read-only. Modules: AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.traffic_state [AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns AMR traffic state text (Cruise/Slow/Stop).
entries.notes: Type: String. Access: read-only. Modules: AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.schedjobs [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the alive ScheduleJobs associated with the OHT Vehicle.
entries.notes: Type: List<ScheduleJob>. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. AMR automatic dispatch does not expose this OHT ScheduleJob list.

entries.title: vehicle.current_schedjob [OHT]
entries.purpose: Gets or selects the current OHT ScheduleJob.
entries.notes: Type: ScheduleJob or null. Access: read/write. Modules: OHT. Only a live job owned by the same Vehicle can be selected.

entries.title: vehicle.battery [AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns AMR battery percentage.
entries.notes: Type: Number. Access: read-only. Modules: AMR. OHT does not expose a battery attribute through this Host.

entries.title: vehicle.blocked_by [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the directly recorded leader/blocker Vehicle, or null when not currently blocked.
entries.notes: Type: Vehicle or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Only the Core-recorded direct blocker is returned. Dependency chains and root cause are not inferred.

entries.title: vehicle.blocked_since_seconds [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns the simulation time this Vehicle began waiting on its current blocked_by, or null when not blocked.
entries.notes: Type: Number (s) or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR.

entries.title: vehicle.blocked_elapsed_seconds [OHT, AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns current simulation time minus blocked_since_seconds, or null when not blocked.
entries.notes: Type: Number (s) or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT, AMR. Computed on read from the existing blocked_since timestamp; no extra polling state is created.

entries.title: vehicle.waiting_for_station [AMR]
entries.purpose: Returns true while the AMR finished loading/unloading but is waiting for its destination Station slot to free.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: AMR. Event-driven: re-evaluated only when the Station frees, not polled.

entries.title: load.id [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the script Load ID.
entries.notes: Type: Number. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: load.name [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the script Load name.
entries.notes: Type: String. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: load.vehicle [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the claimed/onboard Vehicle handle.
entries.notes: Type: Vehicle or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: load.location [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns or supplies the off-Vehicle source/location Station.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read/write. Modules: OHT. Writes participate in pending scripted transport endpoint binding.
entries.related: load.from / load.source aliases are accepted by transport binding

entries.title: load.destination [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns or supplies the active delivery destination Station.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read/write. Modules: OHT. Writes participate in pending scripted transport endpoint binding.
entries.related: load.to / load.target aliases are accepted by transport binding

entries.title: load.onboard [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns true while the Load is physically onboard its carrier.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: load.alive [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns whether the script Load is live.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: load.state [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns created, claimed, onboard, or stored.
entries.notes: Type: String. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. Derived from current script material ownership/location.

entries.title: job.id [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the stable ScheduleJob ID.
entries.notes: Type: Number. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.type [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns current move/retrieve/deliver job type.
entries.notes: Type: String. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.vehicle [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the owning Vehicle.
entries.notes: Type: Vehicle or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.load [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the associated Load for material jobs.
entries.notes: Type: Load or null. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.location [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns or changes the target Station of an uncommitted job.
entries.notes: Type: Number or null. Access: read/write before commit. Modules: OHT. Committed physical jobs reject location rewrites.

entries.title: job.released_us [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns the script release time in microseconds.
entries.notes: Type: Number. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.alive [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns whether the ScheduleJob is live.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.current [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns whether the ScheduleJob is selected as current work.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT.

entries.title: job.physical_committed [OHT]
entries.purpose: Returns true once SimulationEngine already owns the physical route for this ScheduleJob.
entries.notes: Type: Bool. Access: read-only. Modules: OHT. #30 P4: source/destination Station, assigned/pickup/setdown/completed timestamps, and cancel state/reason are Not Implemented as ScheduleJob Attributes -- the current ScheduleJob struct does not own that state, and this Issue does not fabricate a sidecar owner for it.
